atAGlance: Lẩu mắm is Mekong Delta fermented-fish hot pot with seafood, pork, eggplant, and piles of greens. It is a shared-table dish with a deep mắm broth.
whatItIs: Lẩu mắm is a hot pot built on fermented fish broth, usually with river fish or seafood, pork, vegetables, and Mekong-style greens cooked at the table.
howToEnjoy: Cook greens and seafood in stages so the pot stays fresh. Rice noodles or rice help balance the salty fermented broth.
howLocalsOrder: Lẩu mắm is for people who want the deep fermented-fish broth, not a neutral hot pot. Ask what seafood, pork, and wild greens are included, then order rice noodles or vegetables for the table.
worthKnowing: This is one of the clearest Mekong Delta flavors on a menu. The mắm broth is the cultural signal, not a background stock.
goodToKnow: The broth has a strong aroma by design. Order it when the table wants a bold regional hot pot, not a neutral soup.
travelerCaution: Strong fermented fish aroma; often contains seafood and pork.
